question: Using Section 9E.12 and Figure 9E-12, state the minimum bicycle-box length, required pavement symbol, turn-on-red rule, and green-pavement coverage rule.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long (measured from the upstream edge nearest the motor-vehicle stop line to the downstream edge nearest the crosswalk or intersection) and must contain at least one bicycle symbol marking. Turns on red are prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed. If green-colored pavement is used, it must cover the full limits of the bicycle box, and green pavement generally is limited to specified bicycle facilities, including bicycle boxes. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." - "Turns on red shall be prohibited from the lane where a bicycle box is placed." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box." - "If used, green-colored pavement shall be limited to: ... E. Bicycle Boxes (see Section 9E.12), ..." - "Where an existing stop line for motor vehicles is relocated upstream to install a new bicycle box, the yellow change and red clearance intervals (see Section 4F.17) shall be recalculated and if necessary, reprogrammed to accommodate the length of the bicycle box." Guidance (recommended): - A bicycle lane should be used on the approach to a bicycle box. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1 of 2) shows a bicycle box across one lane dimensioned "10 ft MIN." between the intersection stop line and the advance stop line, with bicycle symbol markings in the optional green-colored pavement. [Image 2] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 2 of 2) shows a bicycle box across multiple lanes with optional green-colored pavement covering the full box, bicycle symbols, a "10 ft MIN." dimension, and a NO TURN ON RED (R10-11) sign. [Image 3] Page 1146 presents the Section 9E.12 Standard text stating the 10-foot minimum, the bicycle-symbol requirement, and the turn-on-red prohibition. [Image 4] Page 1147 shows Sheet 1 of Figure 9E-12 with the "10 ft MIN." dimension and the Standard that green pavement shall be used in the full limits of the bicycle box. [Image 5] Page 666 presents Section 3H.06, which limits green-colored pavement to specified bicycle facilities including bicycle boxes. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Standard §9 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Standard §13 (p.1106) - Section 9E.12 Standard §7 (p.1105) - Section 3H.06 Standard §2 (p.626) - Section 9E.12 Guidance §4 (p.1105) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106)
gold_answer: The bicycle box must be at least 10 feet long, include at least one bicycle symbol, prohibit turns on red from its lane, and, if green pavement is used, fill the entire limits of the box.
